with_skill.evidence: First agent message: 'So, first question: why do you want this? What is happening at the gym now that made you want to build it?' No example answers are listed. The first choices offered (own phones as web app / app-store app / gym tablet) come three messages later.

Each agent message puts one thing to the owner: why; 'how long is too long for a route to stay up?'; 'What would make it a failure anyway?'; 'Shall I write it down as the first one...?'; 'Is this right, or what should change?'. Two borderline spots, both judged as one question: the first message phrases the why question twice ('why do you want this? What is happening at the gym now that made you want to build it?'), and the fourth adds 'Say so if you'd rather handle it differently' about the look before its one question. The owner answered one thing each time.

B/work/docs/modules/BRIEF.md, 'Who it is for': 'The gym's setters, on their own phones, at the wall.' Under 'Left out': 'Anything for members: a public route list, ratings, comments, logging climbs.' (marked 'The agent's reading. Not confirmed by the owner.')

BRIEF.md decision 2: 'Setters must be able to use it with no connection, including at the back wall.' with the owner's quote 'It would be a failure if it doesn't work at the back wall, because there's no signal there.'
BRIEF.md decision 4: 'Setters use their own phones, a mix of iPhone and Android, through a web app...'; 'Where it runs': 'In the browser on setters' own phones, iPhone and Android'.

BRIEF.md 'The request' block quotes it exactly: '> I want to build something for my climbing gym so we can keep track of route setting. can you help me figure out what that should be' (string match against first-message.md confirmed).
BRIEF.md decision 1: 'A route is too old once it has been up more than 6 weeks ... The owner, 2026-11-10: "nothing should be up more than 6 weeks"'.

BRIEF.md names no language, framework or database. The one platform form it names, a web app, is recorded as 'Proposed by the agent, and agreed by the owner', which is what happened; hosting of the shared copy is under 'Still open ... The planner chooses'; 'built in Claude Code' is under 'The agent's decisions, not confirmed by the owner'.

BRIEF.md decision 5: 'The owner picks the look from a few visual options, and the first piece of work produces those options.' The only other statement on look is the owner's quote that it 'has to look good'; no description of a look is recorded.

BRIEF.md 'Left out' lists: anything for members (public route list, ratings, comments, logging climbs); scheduling setters, planning resets, hold inventory; reminders or notifications; an app-store app. Payments and competition scoring are not named, and member accounts are covered only loosely by 'Anything for members'. The agent never asked the owner what is left out.

The fifth agent message contains the whole brief between rules, from '# Project brief: route setting tracker' to 'Still open', followed by 'Is this right, or what should change?'. The chat text matches BRIEF.md exactly, and no file is named.

B/work holds only docs/modules/BRIEF.md: no code, module list, milestones or done-when file. The agent defers the rest: 'When you approve, I will commit the brief and start a planning agent on it.' The run ended at the owner's approval.

The agent's five questions are all about the product or the brief's correctness (why, the age rule, what would make it a failure, 'Shall I write it down as the first one: setters use their own phones...?', 'Is this right, or what should change?'). None asks where to save or what to name a file, or whether to continue.
